# Results -- Study 256 (Twitter-Mood) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: join the
curated daily "Calm" mood index (a stylized reconstruction of the GPOMS feed
Bollen et al. used) with real ^GSPC daily returns over the original Bollen
window, regress next-day return on lagged Calm (HAC t), sweep lags 1-5 (the
Granger-lag trap), run a time-shuffle permutation null, the directional
hit-rate vs the unconditional up-rate, and a gross/net long-short trading rule
with a one-day execution lag. **The mood tape is a curated proxy, not the
proprietary feed** -- named on the Signal axis. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| curated Calm index x yfinance ^GSPC daily | 2008-02-28 -> 2008-12-19 | 207 business days | `a8dce11f0ac1` |

Window = the original Bollen, Mao & Zeng (2011) study period (~10 trading
months). n = 207 business days -- far too small to detect a 1-3 day lead-lag
with any statistical power.

## Primary specification -- lead-lag regression (ret_{t+lag} ~ a + b * Calm_t)

| Lag (days) | Slope beta | HAC *t* | R^2 | n |
|-----------|-----------|---------|------|---|
| **1** | +0.00327 | **+0.90** | 0.0043 | 206 |
| 2 | +0.00233 | +0.63 | 0.0022 | 205 |
| 3 | +0.00192 | +0.52 | 0.0015 | 204 |
| 4 | +0.00203 | +0.56 | 0.0016 | 203 |
| 5 | +0.00244 | +0.68 | 0.0024 | 202 |

- The headline one-day-ahead slope is **HAC *t* = +0.90** -- nowhere near the
  *t* >= 2 inference bar. No lag clears even the *uncorrected* bar, let alone
  the Bonferroni bar (|t| ~ 2.58) demanded by sweeping 5 lags.
- R^2 peaks at **0.4%** -- lagged mood explains essentially none of the next
  day's return variance. Bollen's famous "~87% directional accuracy" does not
  survive a clean out-of-sample lead-lag test on this tape.

## Permutation / shuffle null

Time-permuting the Calm series (breaking its alignment with returns) and
re-estimating the slope 2,000 times:

| Lag | Real beta | Real *t* | Permutation *p* |
|-----|-----------|----------|-----------------|
| 1 | +0.00327 | +0.90 | **0.35** |
| 2 | +0.00233 | +0.63 | 0.51 |
| 3 | +0.00192 | +0.52 | 0.57 |

The real slope sits comfortably inside the shuffle null at every lag. There is
no time-alignment between mood and tomorrow's market beyond chance.

## Directional next-day hit-rate vs the honest baseline

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Calm-rule hit-rate | **51.3%** |
| Unconditional up-rate (baseline) | 50.8% |
| Edge over baseline | **+0.5 pts** (n=197) |

The Calm directional rule is statistically indistinguishable from the
unconditional up-rate -- the base-rate trap that flatters every binary market
predictor.

## Trading rule -- gross / net (1-day execution lag, costs on NAV)

| Variant | Gross /yr | Gross *t* | Net @5bps /yr | Net *t* |
|---------|-----------|-----------|---------------|---------|
| Long / flat | +3.9% | +0.17 | +3.2% | +0.14 |
| Long / short | +50.8% | +1.32 | +48.1% | +1.25 |
| Buy-and-hold (window) | -43.1% | -1.18 | -- | -- |

The long-only rule is flat (t = 0.17). The long-short rule *looks* impressive
(+48%/yr net) **only because the window is the 2008 crash**: a rule that goes
net-short during a -43%/yr panic mints money for a reason that has nothing to
do with Twitter mood, and it still **fails to clear t >= 2** (t = 1.25). On
any other window this disappears. Shorts also pay borrow (charged here).

## Positive control -- the machinery finds a lead-lag when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_series`) the same
regression recovers a planted lead-lag and reads ~zero on the null:

| Planted `predictive` | Slope beta | HAC *t* |
|----------------------|-----------|---------|
| 0.000 (null) | -0.00054 | -0.57 |
| 0.002 | +0.00146 | +1.57 |
| 0.004 | +0.00346 | **+3.71** |

The engine works; the real tape simply carries no exploitable mood->market
lead-lag.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Headline lag-1 HAC *t* = +0.90; no lag in the 1-5 sweep
  clears *t* >= 2; permutation *p* = 0.35; directional edge over the
  unconditional up-rate is +0.5 pts. The n = 207 window is far too small to
  detect a 1-3 day effect even if one existed, and the mood tape is a curated
  reconstruction, not the proprietary GPOMS feed. Literature support
  (Bollen 2011) without a robust HAC *t* on the real tape is **WEAK at best**;
  the clean test here returns **NONE**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The only "profitable" variant (long-short, +48%/yr)
  is an artefact of being net-short through the 2008 crash, does not clear
  *t* >= 2, and would not generalize. The long-only rule is flat after costs.
  There is no tradable mood->market edge here.
- **Survivorship -- not applicable** (single index, ^GSPC); **price-only**
  (no dividends, immaterial at a 1-day horizon); both labelled on the Signal
  axis. The headline honesty caveat is the **curated-proxy mood tape** and the
  **tiny n**.
